name: Raja
subject: "Death to Krishnamoorthi"
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch . Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.
Will you chip in $10, $20, or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us elect leaders who won't be intimidated — no matter what they face? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now
Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

Equal Opportunity Now is d/b/a Reviving American Jobs Again PAC (RAJA PAC)

name: Dan Cox
subject: Your Property Tax bill
body:
Marylanders are receiving their property tax bill this week - and the sticker shock for most is no laughing matter. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/coxforcongress/finishing-well-6755722?e=5bb5efcda7)
---
| |
# Your Property Tax Bill Doesn't Have to be That High.
Dear ,

Many Marylanders received their property tax bill this week and the shocking rise in tax due for most is upsetting, if not angering. That's why today we launched our first TV ad also running on social media. [Watch it here](https://us.list-manage.com/Bx6zSQhZiUc?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) and on over 500 channels streaming.

Like two of our older married children, and many like them, so many young families and retirees alike are moving out of Maryland because it is unaffordable for so many. And Wes Moore signed the law to tax them on their way out!

According to research, Maryland is the highest assessment (100%) in the region; and, [Rich States, Poor States](https://us.list-manage.com/h890hmJNLnl?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) has shown that we are one of the highest taxed states in the Nation, ranking near the bottom at 42nd out of 50. But with [your help](https://us.list-manage.com/EP452hQN07n?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) we can change that and continue to reach all of Maryland with our TV ads to beat Wes Moore.

[CLICK AND ](https://us.list-manage.com/1K5G9KJYABz?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)[DONATE HERE TO HELP US WIN](https://us.list-manage.com/17ebrN1x2Sx?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b).
| **State** | **Assessment Ratio** | **Effective Property Tax Rate*** | **Notes**
---|---|---|---
**Maryland** | **100% of assessed value** | **~0.92%** | Full market value assessment statewide.
Pennsylvania | Varies by county (predetermined ratios/common level ratios; generally not 100% of current market value) | ~1.26% | County assessment systems vary significantly.
Virginia | 100% of fair market value | ~0.78% | Localities set tax rates.
Delaware | Fractional assessment system (properties generally assessed using older base-year values with county-specific rates) | ~0.54% | Does not assess at current full market value.
West Virginia | **60% of appraised value** | ~0.51% | Constitutional 60% assessment ratio for real property.
Because Maryland taxes 100% of the _assessed_ value, Governor Moore and his tax assessment office unilaterally raised rates by about 20% for most Maryland homeowners last year simply by raising assessments \- a massive spike on unrealized gains. Now, approximately 30,000 homes are up for tax lien sale this year in our State, and nearly half of those are senior citizens in economically struggling areas such as Baltimore City, Prince George's County and throughout the State.

We can stop this fleecing of Maryland with your help. But it truly is time sensitive - I need your help now.

Sign up to help us win or if you can chip in to keep our ads running, please do. This is a race we can win, but we can't do it alone.

For Maryland,

[](https://us.list-manage.com/uxTSu6MJWKp?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
Dan Cox

body:
Voter Action Project[https://voteractionproject.org/]
Donald Trump is demanding -- again -- that Congress pass the SAVE America Act (the latest version of the anti-voting SAVE Act). With the House set to pass it again this week, the Senate is all we have left to stop this suppressive legislation from becoming law ahead of the midterm elections, folks.

Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on the impact of these bills:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $25 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071126_1&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=071126_1&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=071126_1&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=071126_1&amount=50]

We know the SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before the next election, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
If you missed it: This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $25 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=071126_1&amount=25]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=071126_1&amount=20]

Peter,
Last week, the FBI raided an Ohio voting rights organization and now we just learned they're taking it a step further.
Federal agents descended on the Cleveland office of the Ohio Organizing Collaborative, a grassroots group which has helped hundreds of thousands of Ohioans register to vote. They seized phones and computers from the staff.
They did not stop there. More than 100 agents fanned out across the entire state. They showed up at the homes of organizers and activists tied to the group in Cleveland, Columbus, Cincinnati, Dayton, and Youngstown, and interrogated them about "voter fraud."
No public evidence. No explanation of what the group is even accused of doing. Just federal agents at the doors of people whose only offense is helping their neighbors register to vote. And now we have an alarming update:

The FBI is now expanding the investigation to target the largest progressive voting rights organization, America Votes.
By launching bogus investigations into progressive voting rights organizations, the Trump admin is laying the groundwork for a "voter fraud" conspiracy theory they can use to justify extreme measures to rig the upcoming midterms. This is how a democracy is dismantled. Not all at once, but piece by piece. Raid by raid. Subpoena by subpoena.
Democrats everywhere have to fight back. Our democracy depends on it. Defend Our Courts is leading that charge, and we are fighting on two fronts. First, we are building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections, state by state. Second, we are building the movement to reclaim a United States Supreme Court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration.
[Free and fair elections are under an unprecedented assault by the Trump admin. WILDLIFE IN THE NEWS

“It’s hard not to fall in love with nature when a bald eagle flies over your canoe as you’re paddling down a stream, or when you’re walking a trail and a doe tiptoes by with fawns in tow. That’s what it’s like to explore here; it’s a peaceful immersion into nature.”

Joseph Vaile, Senior Northwest Representative, on the beauty of wildlife refuges in the Midwest.

Read Here → (https://support.defenders.org/s/5745825/38SyG9Xl)

 

Act now: Tell the BLM to keep public lands healthy!

The Bureau of Land Management has proposed changes on public land regulations that could undermine protective regulations and move decision-making behind doors. Public lands belong to all of us – whether you care about hunting and fishing, seeing wildlife, or clean water, you deserve a voice in how these decisions are made! Tell BLM to reject weaker grazing and land health regulations that cut out public feedback! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5745826/38SyG9Xl)

 

Find a National Wildlife Refuge Near You! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5745827/38SyG9Xl)

The National Wildlife Refuge system protects habitat in the Arctic tundra, tropical rainforests, tallgrass prairies – in fact, there’s at least one Refuge in every state. Find out which National Wildlife Refuge is closest to you and which animals you can find there!

body:
Our ability to win statewide is now in serious jeopardy. Republicans just surpassed Democrats in registered voters in Louisiana for the first time in the state’s 214 year history.
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001aqCaz_DUH-tpgloX447fDCY4rZbF_IFn6vRZnSgRlOzBmuwiG8ARu_eBGTCUKBwZftzKs6flBifA_nC58LinTm-olSknEJ4gWcti4lBSV6r5jJOGj-VRrmvcnK_zNPbZuFBOdwjxk97Cn1MFDNXP8VmpkaDTrKMR_x8JJTxPgUnv1pm7e7YVwyFOqPJeSS1N7FNZupYVFnxf5IHK66DxlwrANftHd2LA&c=bdK56QKH8FhLTt6dDo34r-94j9XRpsn--QZpgz22dHqqQ5KSgmV52g==&ch=PccRvbJv-G_JBhhLMgO9cv29FMKi9J5HVg-C5nztQ2W8F1Z7OaXqHA==)

| Peter,
I have an alarming update--and it couldn't come at a worse time.
Republicans just surpassed Democrats in registered voters in Louisiana for the first time in the state's 214 year history.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001aqCaz_DUH-tpgloX447fDCY4rZbF_IFn6vRZnSgRlOzBmuwiG8ARu_eBGTCUKBwZftzKs6flBifA_nC58LinTm-olSknEJ4gWcti4lBSV6r5jJOGj-VRrmvcnK_zNPbZuFBOdwjxk97Cn1MFDNXP8VmpkaDTrKMR_x8JJTxPgUnv1pm7e7YVwyFOqPJeSS1N7FNZupYVFnxf5IHK66Dxl8joBl6Gz1MY&c=bdK56QKH8FhLTt6dDo34r-94j9XRpsn--QZpgz22dHqqQ5KSgmV52g==&ch=PccRvbJv-G_JBhhLMgO9cv29FMKi9J5HVg-C5nztQ2W8F1Z7OaXqHA==)
---
I am not going to lie to you--this is very troubling news. Our voter registration lead has allowed us to win statewide as recently as 2019, when we reelected Democrat John Bel Edwards as governor for a second consecutive term.
And Louisiana has a major U.S. Senate race this November. The Democrat nominee, Jamie Davis, has a real opportunity to pull off a shocking upset and flip LA's senate seat--a win that would all but guarantee Democrats retake the Senate in November.
Due to the backlash against MAGA and the strength of Jamie's campaign, legendary Democratic strategist James Carville has said he believes Democrats have a real "fighting chance" to win this race.
But with Republicans taking the voter registration lead, our ability to win statewide is now in serious jeopardy.
That's why we're launching an emergency initiative to regain the voter registration lead. Starting this month, our No More Silence - Roll to the Polls Tour will see us visit 14 cities across 7 regions with a goal to register 50,000 new voters, recruit No Party voters, and make sure every voter in Louisiana knows how, when, and where to cast a ballot.
The midterm elections are in just 118 days. That's not a lot of time and it's going to take some major resources to regain our voter registration lead.
[That's why we're asking Democrats across the country to pitch in today: Can I count on you to rush a donation of $50, $25, or whatever you can spare to help the Louisiana Democrats register voters, retake the lead, and flip the U.S, Senate blue?](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001aqCaz_DUH-tpgloX447fDCY4rZbF_IFn6vRZnSgRlOzBmuwiG8ARu_eBGTCUKBwZqJHx7k2Ohy-Cn0tJz3sV5pat3x068cQFFV9bavnBT_GzIfHp1Gx5cre3uQ6wMRI6_RB0PxK6pVjDSy0PWhvwHeeZbTK4vizhXIl745__VWpJ99qSQTgypVxv45SDOKk-tAvPhxTLkTIvWgS3o2GGRoFkA1cAXMcNxF_i4XZcDqW5oFmbwQ8cOw==&c=bdK56QKH8FhLTt6dDo34r-94j9XRpsn--QZpgz22dHqqQ5KSgmV52g==&ch=PccRvbJv-G_JBhhLMgO9cv29FMKi9J5HVg-C5nztQ2W8F1Z7OaXqHA==)

## Four Subpoenaed for Air Force One Report
The Trump administration [subpoenaed four _New York Times_ journalists](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQRp8Gd0SAf3AKim3c3W23tMZmCJPFYMEkUd5-lV3tE9z6kz6dc359rV9AifLtJxzoOJQ146slZMa6-nJvj-0smKFVPEtlrC2WbVuNMpNUVmqzeqD0XofOu4BosO_QaTv386jmwXTRWT-BCTtob3cTBkQfRqX7uVdB-20aOnKfN2W10UpZfb2EUV9htzAH62GAIAaFnrjUy71Q5oghvcsT62UvR5dcZD6b6H8IswizcMRIKX02YZZYDvwICbMc6AmEWcbr1M9aS44oM77ku9TfkunAJu_lUTMkatzkf3EJVGUodUdZMkqqkCXHisDyXxJhlq46f74oJWqTFYO6HUB_CTr-VtKnM38CAAD__-_NjfU) on Friday, after a story that outlined the risks involved in flying the Qatar-gifted Air Force One plane that recently entered into service. The report questioned whether the new plane, a Boeing 747-8, had been ["retrofitted with sufficient security measures"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAURL8Gd0RwTQIuKF5Dl9duaV2HS0yEjQUkkf9-5dXu_sDWMzqaMx_X8YoxxfX-HxeyLeRxpXdN1BqV0edHfU5bphVroS2XRqXOeZpGEHDhQnMJo8eY9lF13gYioL4jK7XpzVkYBd1sB1BCDVoQkjZnhVoF43EYpj6ACaLvoj1oQkuQQmg5nMJZDnjTaIL2qDAwJcjHlsvpkePaZgppzy8qp1teumTn1rbK-n8MHAO37luu7YgYuAPMwAnNwEnJwD0rP_wYuBYXqvzXiv-IkucYGhWOsfCQy414Xum7yMB1xfrtHVOK9aKZEvcFY_pa0v5038vCZwAAAP__J4-ETQ) during the rush to get it in the air. The president [flew the new Air Force One to a NATO summit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ8GOke2-RkoXNwmXW67JRrsmeDIYNZMEuXtV-wrbHl0pKPzfV-36YYxxe3-H1dywnna6H0kEqEyhfw4nvOeacOj0J6LUDmWPM-T1bZXGpSxU8CYPlNbB8dElpqanIGhGTo9tLZeHEBnPHBviDWz19hbxn5uOAydN11TR3euaTDWaA1mvHBnRvSAA0PAFrlqNYUouVweOW6yEKdPflG5-LzWyS0i-1E1_yp7rewV9xPgrM5QJPpElb1Kea672j6iMBbFuXhSeSP1jYIlqgeJIuthHHDs0FBrNECwHmnsR4A28Gjq4sL-jinFo4eq1fcVY_r9IH8S93L2JwAA__8EKoIL) in Turkey last week. But he departed on Wednesday on one of the older-model Air Force One jets for a trip to England before switching to the newer plane for the flight home to Joint Base Andrews. The _New York Times_ reported that the switch had come [at the urging of the Secret Service](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAcxJ8GOwz-wUULiq-x26-90oD8WdkgGMA1vv3FS-4JrptkMjP5zddzfmoffHz91xuq6tIc8SwBa8U82_Quh9kTRl0y7ilXzGVNxszA4EGZpB3MVvtwzaKxyiEC8gZVJwc-9GwQ0KxK8N4ww-WDMxDD2EsrOFipR7M4No6m8epuY7KDjjHZja3ru1EvUg9OWi20I4Kh9TXl9p18rCu6cKUP5nZJWxPUWuteCP9HYCIwnefZLqbcFLdPYLolganmY9up9pm6lBekKSItuBzZ14v-YtJ3OnLUwZd6Z5qs7H76EHx5SCLYa9M-_MzWP331UfAdAAD___9jgC0). Another article indicated that the newer plane lacked some of the advanced security features of the older aircraft, including antimissile capabilities. Both reports cited anonymous sources.
## Most of US Faces Dangerous Heat This Week
A dangerous [heat wave will build across the U.S.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOiL_gU3h4jbpctst0bF9TnBkMLK9QXn7FfsKW45GmtH3fT2WB8QU9-d_2NA2ysuOZ03YGpYl5Ff9dkfGHWrBI5eGpa7ZuUUwMQ1MD1wsAWL6LKoPlhAFyh4t10aakRkl-tXOTIwzIuqJlAc1c_Tc8MBQEfd8FH201xrTXHDGNJ9vNPIZvAZDOoAC6hTDEFsut1eOe1uR0ie_sdx83vpk19aO2sl_nbh34g7HBXBVVygt-oSduK8IbTjhjUPIGw4nQluxDIYZbTRpCZMC9I7ISamcIu9ISjf1xYbjjCnFOulOsecGMf3-tj_JelvxEwAA__-kPn3Z) this week with triple-digit highs expected to spread from the Southwest to the East Coast. High humidity will increase [the risk of heat-related illnesses](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SrCAQhZ8GMy1of8CA4CZkc9MNrVaakSkUC5ixfPstN9kH2Li_6vOd8_WYHuiD35__cSNdXJx2OnOgUihNNr7yez4i7ZgTHTEVSnmN8zwBh6HmshYwWfThmrrKakcE1FakhVSt6rnqoFq1VQMORGpeRjuMore8bUe02NmFS2ex8vr-xqUAwbkUY-N6MeIiUTlpsUPHOk7Wl5iaV_R7WcmFK34oNUvcqqDXUo7M2n8MDANznmfzzliixesGGJhcYroYmLvZTRCWlRIDc-cyMFwyMEL8nmoXEy2YS70SltrGjRiYkSspe3VLMjBV0vY4fQg-D5J1_LmhDz9G5U8zfjR8BwAA__-ulIVY), and locations in the Rockies and northern Plains could approach the hottest temperatures on record. In California, temperatures near 100 degrees sparked [a fast-spreading blaze in Los Angeles County](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ_G7hzxa0xBsU26bLuldQyH-EQELCCJ8vYr31e45Wik0Xzfv9t6A0qU73_hia7Hsmb8tIS9Y11DebTXdhTM0CoepXasbS_btgom5omZiYs1AKXvqsbgIqJAOaLjZpGLZosS4-6YtEbOYM3CvZ-VBa55UMxw5rVVEUdy5xozXHDGDLeXqLkFb2CJJoCCOCiGgXqpl0eh3HeM6VveWC--PMfk9t6PNsg_g7gO4grHCXBWZ6idfMJBXD0kiqVmgulDKUSqOKXSJsh3TNgmX165fyepF0Q5ayY2pmcv5cwsRFBRhmCi1WN14fhQStRmMyh2fwKlnx_9V_LeTvwPAAD__xxGgtw) that covered 2,700 acres on Friday. Meanwhile, [hundreds of people were rescued on Friday in Missouri](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkk1v6joQhn9N2AU5zvcii7SQCy3QXiiXj43l2JPE1InBdpILv_6I6qzO9uxmntE80mjew5qsqZCiqze0hcxWinQwGgnWgiZcXUxfXhV01Gi4Km1Bm0aVJcEIRy6KXQ8TToW8k2DCswoAgz-BzIsTPwlREuBJkyXMS0Lq45hyjiKIkyr1eRD6EWcU-0E4EdnThmIPewjFXjqtQi-lLKZJFXMa0MoJEHBhlZ5elOhsA5W8qwH0lKl2IrPG2qtx_NzBhYOLcRynd9oo9Zw6uHie88RAbQPa_d1SbQWT8CxbYYzqtXDrp7NT2uXAJNVgXGOpBRda0DV07O56aYAwRok3bWwrHb-oe8ZU31nQjj_zHBzVPQOioQKtfxhdbBFbrKPVPe3PR_5YtXwoMTfnXXgpMRr-XCFG1I4_y__N83yRLx_b9-X2kpdv16LcJ8lR5pzjxesumv13POWf87XdHLg8iuDlA3iQHuf8ZTCnnUvQpqi47v7nF_LxVh2-bzvBxjRavuaf72_qthwQJ-1peJy_k5i0kMbn7cLLwyVZ5i96P6sKtaftvL2Fds_Ws69PbwySpHv0K_d2U_98tfPN1v-Qq06fzpv5QU50xq-jkFKYKHYCVLdUyJ_32L_K1JDhXwEAAP__QKDjQQ) amid rapidly rising floodwaters, following intense storms in several regions across the state.

**Whatever happened to Tang?** In 1957, General Foods cooked up a concoction of orange "flavor crystals" that the company named Tang. It hit shelves two years later as a vitamin-fortified instant breakfast drink, and almost nobody bought it. Then NASA came calling. The agency needed something lightweight, shelf-stable, and strong enough to mask the taste of recycled spacecraft water, and Tang fit the bill. When astronaut John Glenn sipped it aboard _Friendship 7_ in 1962, General Foods pounced, slapping launch pads on the canisters and sponsoring ABC's coverage of Apollo 8. Kids everywhere begged for "the astronaut drink." Here's one of [the early space commercials](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OKiEYxvGrYTonfClYUJhzYrKFW21iOXmBF8HgMAvoxLvfzN7Cts-T_Ir_9TJdIOU03z7hgaaHMs24toy9Y518ubenXQrO0CoupXasLRZrJ075YUfVjvHJQ8rvSQ7eBESOYkDDlBZ6T7XkQzTKSa2OSrCg92CpdQ6FhuCZDA6ohCGZTaOKcUapYscx7NkRnAIdlAcJgUiKPvVSx3tJc48Y8ru8sI6uPIZsYu9LI-JE-Jnw87qu47s8-9Pi9m8LdBeJOL-I-P91vcV__uMb_Wmoxi9ryjm1gyKS3h6Q8i_Z_9ThZfhPAAAA__9DoHKr), and [here's a later one](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1q6zAYxvGrkbYYfTmyBw0HDllKCoW0HcUr61WsIFtGUmJy9yW9ha7PA7_h_322Z4gprtd3WNC0kO2Ke03YGhbr863e3ZZxhVpwy6VhqXN2zgomjgemD1xYDzE9raLeBESBkqLhepBDzwYl6Gw0jFo6DtxzqZzm_ejA61H1EwSvAqfRvDSmueCMaT52oecjTBqGoD0oCEQx9LHl0t1yXNuMIT3zA0s35YUmM7e2VSL_EXEi4rTve_fM93Z3-PpfC7RpJvL0IPL_x-VT1bev5XLMtBi_7TGlWI-aKHZdIKZfsv2pw8OInwAAAP__2AtyDQ). But what goes up must come down, and by the late 1980s, parents were reaching for Capri Sun pouches and juice boxes, and Tang, packing 29 grams of sugar a glass, started gathering dust. A late 90s [orangutan mascot couldn't save it](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6yAUxvGngS0WHIhxBoYr3UQZmg5dOiIMh5iIGAtILL995b5C1--TfsP_-2ZuNqY43z_tE3UL2cy41oStYTE-P-prXDLOthZccmlY6pTH0QCD_sDUgYPxNqbNSOp1QAQUFDVXgxiObJBAJx08KN9z2R8Vk8iAcT46iwGccGLggUa9a0xx4IwpfurCkZ-sU3YIyltpA5EMfWy5dI8c5zZhSFt-Y-lcftKkp9aWSsQ_AhcCl3Vduy2_2mvE_d8X29xExOVNxP_-4_zlT9cZr2datF_WmFKsvSKS3Z82pl-y_anDW8NPAAAA__-GWXGF). But here's the twist: while Americans moved on, the rest of the world didn't. Tang shifted its focus to developing markets, and by 2011, it was a [billion-dollar global brand](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGSgyAQgOGnwU5nWTVoQXGNXa690llhiWSIOEDC5O1vcq9w_T9f8f9c1yv54I_bNz1YFxfXg2sOXAqn1cZ7fm5n5INy4jOmwinvcdtWBLy0oFqJqyUf3uvQWO2YkfuGtVRTP40wDdjs2m52Vmx6kPNIYNDMsIFzYy8N9HaUjdcfDZRECaDk3LlRzmQUTU5ZGsiJAdj6ElN3j_4oO7vwji9OnYmPJui9lDOL_kvgInCptXZmj3WPz8N-CoGLVAqmyyhw8bktdNzaXHwILaVPJHBpkrZn9SH4fFFigNuDfPjjy7-evDT-BgAA__8Bp3W6), fueled by Brazil, Argentina, the Philippines, and the Middle East, where more than half of annual sales happen in the six weeks around Ramadan. In 1957, General Foods cooked up a concoction of orange "flavor crystals" that the company named Tang. It hit shelves two years later as a vitamin-fortified instant breakfast drink, and almost nobody bought it. Then NASA came calling. The agency needed something lightweight, shelf-stable, and strong enough to mask the taste of recycled spacecraft water, and Tang fit the bill. When astronaut John Glenn sipped it aboard Friendship 7 in 1962, General Foods pounced, slapping launch pads on the canisters and sponsoring ABC's coverage of Apollo 8. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. ## NTSB Details Deadly Laredo Jet Crash
Both engines on a business jet flamed out on final approach to Laredo, forcing the crew to crash-land on a highway, a preliminary [National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) report](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O4zAMBeDT2J0CkVakqHCxjbvZdkuDluixdugfSEo8uf0i2SNMSRB4D9_78zF-UJK0ff6mlfv6Pe_jxmcRrpXz-Hcvy50m4hwylSXzseeaWXhEjVZppwDHSEmeo2ljP-nooeUe3K27XQ0Y2y797GIXGHyY55nRsGV9DUQwO2NR-2ub-leYdoAAGtFcEKyLQRvjJujA-sZojqnu-VIXrvxNZZbn_uB8CfvaSr_UepSm-9Xg0OBwnufl63Hn17PBgXJNQbjB4eVqcJA9kLzOWiZ1ZJa0po3yU_3XKaHMcVfvHnUIbazeePWVRDgqupeaNjXdS9q4lJW2Bge0XkVnonFTp9gDKAPeK28DKbg5jhDijbRpcx-PM4mkYl1j9OdKSd6M-rPxHz3-CwAA___dW5lm) released Friday found. The NetJets-operated jet was flying from Los Cabos, Mexico, to Austin on June 16 when the crew noticed an "unusual vibration." Warnings of low fuel pressure and cascading failures followed as it neared the border. Cleared to divert to Laredo International, the jet lost its right engine on approach and then its left. A controller said their only option was "the main highway," and they set down on Loop 20, shearing light poles and hitting a pickup. The crash killed [Joshua Baer](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHS2yAMgJ8Gb8ohmZpk8NDF29-1o08EOSbFkAPyO3n7ntNH6KzT90nf76_5i0MM6faLNxnba8lzkr1GaU3KfM91fbJjKdfCdS3yyKUViTKTpgG0BaTZc4jv2XR-dNpfsJMR7bk__zBohm4dDaMT78Xbfjl711tEvvBAbuGBNLoujAdMWyRETWROhIP1V22MddjjcFFGiw8tl1NbpcmL6xLf-VvK6Zq3Lo5ra4-q-p-KJkXTvu-nP5XbMVQ0Hd8omj5riqZDpWjSVtGEqGhyua0g6RaSVFgib-IhPxs4WXIRqBvHCHdp8CkgHkKC-zMJ5AQfKKzhtu78htSqg3-JoPL7sHVl9I89xBjqYJXRt41D_Fzd_q_190h_AwAA__80PJSL), the Austin entrepreneur who founded Capital Factory. subject: Something has to matter more than just profits.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
We do not have to accept this.
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=22%2E42639%2E-XhV2b)
We do not have to accept this.
We do not have to accept the corruption and trickle-down economics that has stabbed at the heart of my district and communities across the country.
We do not have to accept corporations chasing the cheapest labor and weakest environmental rules and the lousy trade deals that send good jobs overseas.
We do not have to accept the endless pursuit of corporate profits at any cost.
**[Something has to matter more than just profits. Please watch:](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/257?t=2&akid=22%2E42639%2E-XhV2b)**
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/257?t=3&akid=22%2E42639%2E-XhV2b)
But if we are going to fundamentally change our economy into one that puts the hard work at its center, then we have to do more than just be anti-Trump.
We have to show what we are willing to do if Democrats take back the House and the Senate... and then we have to do it.
We have to root out the corruption in Washington wherever we see it. We've got to ban Congressional stock trading.
In the richest country in the history of the planet, people should have health care: We should pass Medicare for All.
There's nothing more corrupt than the money in our politics, we've got to get the super PAC money out of our elections.
Democrats took on the robber barons once before with the New Deal.
We broke their stranglehold on politics.
We can do it again.
But we have to have fight in us to get it done.
Know that I have that fight in me.
In solidarity,
Chris Deluzio

* * *

That promise doesn't preserve itself.
[This year, it's on the ballot in Ohio and across America.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.__KQ)
You've seen what's happened elsewhere. New York just elected a self-described socialist mayor. Virginia just elected a Democrat running on the same bigger-government agenda. That same radical movement is now just one election away from reaching Ohio.
[I'm not going to pretend this is a normal election, because it isn't.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._)
This election will determine whether the next generation of Americans grows up believing they can build something with their own two hands, or believing the government exists to build it for them.
Those are two fundamentally different visions for our country.
One is rooted in freedom, personal responsibility, and the American Dream. The other replaces opportunity with dependence and individual ambition with government control.
I know which future I want for my children. And I know it's the future worth fighting for.
That's why I'm asking for your help today, Peter.

Peter, when the Vice President came to North Carolina to attack me by name, **I knew we were in for a long race.**
When President Trump followed up a few weeks later with a late-night Truth Social post attacking me again, **I knew they were nervous.**
Now, after President Trump’s attack dog Stephen Miller went on Fox News to rant and rave about me, **I can tell we’re getting to them.**
There are a lot of important Senate races happening this year, but President Trump knows that if they just win in NC, it’ll stop our chances of taking back the Senate. It won’t matter what happens in other swing states – if the GOP wins NC, that’s the ballgame. They’ll likely keep Senate control until 2029.
That’s why we’re facing these nonstop attacks, and why I’m emailing you today. If we can’t hit our fundraising goals, it’ll make it much harder to run the ads we need to win – and this is a race we just can’t afford to lose.

body:
I’ll be honest, Peter.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260712_1_holder.CqLvRM&refcode=em20260712-1540&amount=5&t=1&akid=1540%2E299639%2Ej7y88e)
Peter,
I’ve spent much of my career fighting to protect the foundations of our democracy — from defending voting rights as the 82nd Attorney General of the United States to working to protect the voice of the people in elections across the country.
Through my experience, I've learned that the fights that matter most for the future of our nation often happen at the state level. And to be honest, the stakes in Texas right now couldn’t be higher.
Recently, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled to severely weaken key protections from the Voting Rights Act that historically helped communities of color fight back against rigged maps. And Greg Abbott has used every single move he has in his pocket to redraw district lines and lock in power for Republicans, and he will continue to do so – only emboldened by the Supreme Court’s disastrous decision – if we don’t stop him.
We need you to understand exactly what this means for the future of our country.
Before I explain, **[will you make a $5 donation to Gina Hinojosa’s campaign today to ensure she is elected this November and can finally put an end to this corruption?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260712_1_holder.CqLvRM&refcode=em20260712-1540&amount=5&t=2&akid=1540%2E299639%2Ej7y88e)**
Texas is growing at a rapid pace. By the next census, the state is projected to gain 3 to 4 more congressional seats. This means Texas is going to carry even more weight in the House and the electoral college.
If Republicans hold on to unchecked control of Texas through 2030, they’ll draw maps so extreme that it will become nearly impossible for Democrats to win a majority in Congress – even if that’s what a majority of Americans want.
_That is why this governor’s race is so important._
**We must elect governors who have the courage to veto these rigged, anti-democratic maps.** If Texans elect Gina, she will stand as a vital roadblock against partisan overreach, stopping the next Republican gerrymandering stunt and protecting a fair playing field for the entire country.
I’m proud to support such an impressive candidate, who will fiercely advocate for every Texan’s rightful representation. **[But she can’t do it alone. Peter, will you chip in $5 today to help elect Gina and bring true leadership back to Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260712_1_holder.CqLvRM&refcode=em20260712-1540&amount=5&t=3&akid=1540%2E299639%2Ej7y88e)**

Thank you,
Eric H. Holder, Jr.
82nd United States Attorney General

| | Peter,
This year, as we mark 250 years in this great experiment in liberty, I keep asking myself the same question: _**Are we keeping the faith?** _
Let me explain what I mean.
At the very heart of it, _we were born a nation of Christian pilgrims and dissenters. _
The Pilgrims. The Puritans. The Quakers. The Huguenots. The German Pietists. Wave after wave of men and women who crossed an ocean because they refused to let any earthly power stand between them and their biblical faith in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob – the God revealed in Jesus Christ.
_That is the seed America grew from_ , and every time we’ve forgotten this, we’ve gone astray.
The very first freedom in the Bill of Rights – the one the framers put first, not fifth or tenth, but first – is **the freedom to worship God without interference from government**. That wasn’t random. It was the whole point.
And when people knock our founding fathers as relics of a bygone era who “wouldn’t understand the world today,” I ask you to think about our brothers and sisters in Christ today, _right now_ , in places like Nigeria, Iran, Pakistan, North Korea and many other places.
**There are an estimated 388 million Christian men, women and children being persecuted, oppressed and ruthlessly murdered simply for loving Jesus.**
Here in America, _it’s almost impossible to know what that’s like_ , but we do have the freedom, the platform and the resources to support them, and fight back in a wide range of ways. **The question is, will we?**
I can’t help but feel that this year, on the 250th birthday of the world’s most indispensable Christian nation, that we have a duty to rededicate ourselves to God and to the defense of His people around the world. **And today, I’m asking you to partner with me and an incredible organization in that endeavor.**
**There is no organization in this country more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians, where I’m proud to serve as a board member.** ** ** Whether it’s the growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America, it is due in very large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide.
[ **As we commemorate America’s 250th birthday, I humbly but urgently ask that you help to supercharge their efforts with a generous, tax-deductible contribution.** ](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=be4621b4cfcb4042acc321e78195a705&_e=Jo3jk0cVFttY-4c7pP-PD8sRkHBhjR2uEslVT9oqu5hf0SajbJbfYgVtJWIwnSZ_rHvSQAP_oEKRZAocqQtF5zB6D96HGPkIm_dXJBYcZDAZOpg56_jxI0vY1i4D0U2R-1r7J3XacNWW-8HTbx_Jp8ukz5wFEiCh8f8-cfc8I2oAo2DRF-gEGLOZn0uxMZ7dA98e-6P3kQFuUWgEUwC6I59jGVWsTj_sTTfcp6uqQ9tQwtH0BZWvnIB-BDKGfy8fGGa--6ImtyReFh6TzizOw2VeZZXddrX2EEINkEoH86MU9rayirS7bItP7FT7mz-ySrOpY8i8XQdB1E9oMvZlft8Txk4qTbD393S0uHRVzT41WaE3goTwZ0aAJpzOCsY4_lPsiPLCeHj1bxrku1xzAWx1jbLX_Q9HZh43C5uiXbEOpJyd48LAoXt9ITGvabmzNALVaCANcvxg6mq4Nc9rVxv8V0go-XzDnTgU_1tk6Q7w3kqySnpLhJJ3ng8PSEH5LIr7Zb3MVeSi4HdPvd2-GVeLpyVBM3BP9E-y14wjEnLYHtDMwltJ2Psu3_7gVWNoffrXtuG7oZ30t_4hxW1ytUWcR3aYfekEJkrumeeTd9QhSyTHW378jYm64V6xZKNEEGzoXJRu741FIL42JpuaM9KclPidJUCBsQtOpIW-eRu0tjzcX41usXn8Cr_lX669Z7oJnr1aA1EsKD23MwWghU_Iu7ni6gmQADOreMryHrvnpDItm1hpyEtAsmp1p8xoUk9gyMy6dOID4uHsXA82rQ%3D%3D)

As you contemplate your potential commitment, I ask you to think about this.
**While Christians in America today are the freest Christians in the history of the world, 388 million of our brothers and sisters, in other parts of the world, are being hunted for practicing the same faith that built this country.**
Every generation that ever mattered to the kingdom of God understood that faith without action is sentiment – and sentiment has never freed a single soul.
**Now it's our turn.**
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the founders pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor. _They paid the price._ They handed us the inheritance. The only real question this year is what we do with it.
On July 3, 1776 – one day after the Continental Congress had voted to declare independence – John Adams sat down in Philadelphia and wrote to his wife Abigail.
He told her this new American holiday " _ought to be commemorated, as the Day of Deliverance, by solemn Acts of Devotion to God Almighty. It ought to be solemnized with Pomp and Parade, with Shews, Games, Sports, Guns, Bells, Bonfires and Illuminations, from one End of this Continent to the other, from this Time forward forever more._ "
Notice the order. _First solemn devotion to God._ Then the fireworks.
250 years later, we’ve kept the fireworks. But the question is, have we maintained the devotion?
I believe we still can. **This anniversary is bigger than a birthday party. It is a reckoning** – with our history, with our blessings, and with our obligations to the brothers and sisters around the world who are paying the highest possible price for the very faith we still get to practice openly.
They are praying for a Church that does not always remember their names.
On this 250th birthday – of all years – we have the chance to tell them they are not forgotten.
[ **That is what your gift does. That is what Save the Persecuted Christians does. ---
| | Fellow Patriot,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260712-1-b&t=1&akid=11624%2E3935704%2EbZejPn)

Hi friends,
It’s Gabby Giffords, and I need to be candid with you.
As you read this, the Trump administration is taking dangerous actions to roll back our progress on gun safety.
* They’re rolling back dozens of gun regulations, including restoring gun rights to some people who were deemed mentally unfit to own guns.
* They’re pressuring the U.S. Postal Service to overturn its 99-year ban and allow handguns to be delivered through the mail.
* Now, Donald Trump himself announced that he’s working to pass a nationwide concealed carry mandate.

Donald Trump called himself the NRA’s “best friend” — and now it is clear that he’s doing all he can to make sure his gun lobby buddies can get richer.
**[We cannot stand for this. Will you pitch in $10 right now to help GIFFORDS PAC hold Republicans accountable at the ballot box? Your donations will help us share our message with undecided voters.](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-q32026.dTscjt&refcode=em260712-1-b&t=2&akid=11624%2E3935704%2EbZejPn)**

Look, it can be easy to forget that gun violence is happening around us every day. But for the families who’ve lost loved ones, they can never, ever forget.
The November election will be our best opportunity to elect a gun sense majority and hold Donald Trump accountable, but it won’t be easy. The gun lobby will spend millions of dollars to drown out our message and keep the system rigged in their favor.
So I am asking, humbly:

When I started my first business, I prayed it would be successful... God answered.

[](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDcxMl9JTC1DWC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NTA5MjQtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA3MTJfSUwtQ1guMTEwMTE3X3QxOTUwOTI0LTI4OTkifQ/XjwaLImLdv21Q3XGPICnMA)God works in mysterious ways...
When I started my first business, I prayed it would be successful... **God answered.**
When I was deployed to Afghanistan, I prayed my family would be safe... **God answered.**
When I saw career politicians turn their backs on Americans to put their pet projects before the interest of the American people, I prayed for a better outcome...
I was surprised when **_God called on ME_** to run for office.
I'm Troy Downing. You might not recognize my name, but that's okay.
I'm a combat veteran. A God-fearing Christian. A husband & a proud dad.
**[I'm also the Republican running for re-election in Congress for Montana in the biggest race in the country.](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDcxMl9JTC1DWC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NTA5MjQtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA3MTJfSUwtQ1guMTEwMTE3X3QxOTUwOTI0LTI4OTkifQ/52Wss3VaLjfKNHWZDeAZuQ)**
I'm not in this to become a household name or for the title. I don't care about any of that.
I'm a simple man who enjoys a beer, likes to hunt and fish with my buddies & puts my family before anything else.
**__But I'm at my wits' end with two-faced politicians and DC bigwigs who say one thing to your face, only to turn around & stab hard-working folks like you & me in the back.__**
I'll always tell the truth. I'll always put America first. I'll always stand up for what's right.
The Radical Left will spread lies about me & throw me under the bus just to end my campaign before the midterms.
**[Peter, can you take a leap of faith on a simple combat vet like me to beat the Left & save our country?](https://trk.emails.troydowning._bW9uZXlfcGxlZGdlPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTUwJmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDcxMl9JTC1DWC4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NTA5MjQtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA3MTJfSUwtQ1guMTEwMTE3X3QxOTUwOTI0LTI4OTkifQ/dsVrykEjR-vM9AmIta83Qg)**[HELP A COMBAT VET

Troy Downing (R-MT)| |

Pete Hegseth is playing favorites and passing over qualified Black and female servicemembers for promotions, and targeting them for demotion and dismissal—while also promoting inexperienced MAGA loyalists.
Nearly 60 percent of the senior officers fired by Hegseth are female or Black. Women and racial minorities in our military have been denied promotions, baselessly fired or dismissed, or have been pushed out of the ranks at alarming and unprecedented rates.
Rewarding loyalty to MAGA above the experience, expertise, and exemplary service of the men and women who have dedicated their lives to our country is both despicable and dangerous.

subject: What happens now in Maine:
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
This week, we called on our own nominee for the U.S. Senate to withdraw. We hold every candidate who seeks to carry our banner to the highest standard, and we stand with women and survivors. That principle does not bend based on party affiliation.
He has now withdrawn.
The hard decision in this story was not ours. It belonged to the women who came forward, because speaking up is often costly, and we respect them for it.
Our responsibility required judgment and a willingness to act when circumstances demanded it. Circumstances demanded it. We acted.
Now we want to talk to you about what happens next, because it matters enormously.
There is no Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Maine.
Our party will come together, as our rules provide, to choose the Democrat who will carry our banner against Susan Collins. We will do it carefully and we will do it right. Mainers deserve nothing less.
But here is the hard truth about that gap:
Susan Collins does not pause while we confer. She has been raising money for this race for six years. Her campaign is raising more today, and it will raise more tomorrow. The corporate PACs and wealthy interests her votes protect are not waiting to see who our nominee is. They are adding to a war chest six years in the making, while our side has no candidate, no campaign, and no one answering. Whoever we choose will start this race six years behind.
Every day of this holding period is a day she banks money unanswered.
We refuse to let our next nominee start from zero.
So the Maine Democratic Party is opening the Day One Fund: money raised now, held ready, so that the moment our new nominee is chosen, they inherit a running start instead of an empty account.
Day one, they will need a statewide organizing operation already paid for.
Day one, they will need voter contact already underway in all 16 counties.
Day one, they will need to answer Collins on the air, not spend a month catching up.
That is what this fund does. Not a bailout, not a rainy-day account. A running start, waiting for whoever earns the nomination. Can you help power us with a split contribution between Maine Democrats and Equal Opportnity Now today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY TO THE DAY ONE FUND! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
This Senate race comes at a pivotal moment in the struggle against a government, supported by Senator Collins, that serves the interests of the wealthy and powerful at the expense of ordinary Maine people. That struggle did not end this week. If anything, our responsibility to it grew.
The party will do its job in the days ahead. We are asking you to do yours today, so that our nominee, whoever they are, walks into this fight ready. Will you chip in a split contribution between Maine Dems and Equal Opportunity Now today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
CHIP IN BEFORE OUR NOMINEE IS CHOSEN! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-medems]
Thank you for your support,
The Maine Democrats

Twelve people. A courtroom. A stranger's freedom in their hands.
We do this constantly, and we've done it so long we've stopped noticing how radical it is. We reach into ordinary life and pull out twelve ordinary people -- the nurse, the mechanic, the retired schoolteacher - and there should be a taco truck driver too -- and we hand them a power that would make most of us dizzy: the power to decide whether another human being walks out of that room free, or spends years of their life in a cage.
We don't ask whether they campaigned for it. We don't check their resumes. We don't see who funded them, because nobody funded them. We simply trust them -- because underneath the whole solemn architecture of the jury is a very old and very radical belief about regular people: that given the facts, the time, and a real obligation to reason together, they will mostly find their way to something like justice.
We stake a person's liberty on that belief every single day.
And then we turn around and act as if those same people couldn't possibly be trusted to weigh in on the tax code.
## **Let me say the awkward part out loud**
You'd be right to notice something. I am running for Congress. I am asking you to send me to Washington DC. ## **Half one: who 's in the room**
There's an old word for the first half. It sounds technical, so let me introduce it, set it down and then mostly leave it alone: _sortition_. Selection by lot. It means you choose the people who deliberate not by election, but by a civic lottery -- exactly the way we already choose juries.
The process is not "random" in the way that word is used to scare you. We don't just yank 535 names out of a hat. (Although, do you think we might actually have a more representative legislature, even if we only did that?)
Sortition uses a "stratified lottery," which is a fancy phrase for a simple thing: you draw names in such a way that the room ends up looking like the country. Renters and homeowners. A welder, a nurse, a farmer, a schoolteacher, a lawyer, a landscaper, a kid three years out of high school sitting next to a grandmother three years into retirement. Rural and urban. Black, white, brown. Immigrant, native-born. Every income. Every background.
Above all, the people who would never in a thousand years _run for office_ -- the caregivers, the tradespeople, the night-shift workers, the working parents... the quietly competent people who hold this whole country together and have no interest whatsoever in becoming a brand.
They become legislators, for a set period of time. And they are treated like the public servants they are. They're paid for their time. Childcare, transportation, interpretation, disability access, are all covered-- so that serving isn't a luxury only the comfortable can afford.
They're given a domain, a policy question, some thorny topic that affects their lives and their communities. They're provided balanced briefings and access to experts who openly disagree with each other. They hear directly from the communities their decision will impact the most.
And then they're given the one thing our politics almost never allows anyone: **time**. Time to learn, to question, to discuss, to seek out more evidence, to change their minds, and to eventually arrive at a decision they'll have to stand behind.
That's it. That's the first half. It answers exactly one question -- who's in the room? -- and it answers it in a way that **money and entrenched interests cannot get out in front of**. Lobbyists and corporate interests cannot spend five years cultivating a legislator whose name won't exist until the day she's drawn.

## **Half two: how the room actually works**
But a room full of well-chosen people can still become the worst meeting you've ever sat in. Anyone who's survived an HOA board, a PTA fight, or a city-council public-comment night knows that "gathering good people" and "governing well and making good decisions together" are not _remotely_ the same thing.
So the second half matters just as much -- and this is the part I know from lived experience, not just theory.
It's called **sociocracy**. It's a way of coordinating group actions and making decisions together that I've worked inside professionally, running real teams and real budgets on complex projects reaching millions of dollars.
This sounds like an exaggeration and simply is not: **sociocracy is the most humane -- and honestly the most fun -- way of getting hard things done that I have ever been part of.**
The bones of it are these: People speak in rounds -- you go around the circle, every voice, one at a time -- so the loudest, most aggressive person in the room can't run the table, and the quietest person can't be steamrolled or just quietly forgotten.
Decisions aren't made by crude majority, where 51 crush 49 and the 49 walk out resentful and already plotting the next fight. They're made by **consent**. And consent has a beautiful, practical definition. Not "everyone loves it." Not "everyone agrees it's perfect."
Just:** "good enough for now, and safe enough to try."**
And it directly answers what we've all experienced, and dread-- the one stubborn soul who blows up the whole evening by refusing to budge. "Consent" mode is precisely what disarms that person.
Because an **objection** , in sociocracy, isn't a tantrum, and it isn't a veto you get to swing around the room. An objection is _information_ : a reasoned explanation that "this will actually harm the work, or harm my ability to do the thing I'm responsible for."
When someone raises a real objection, the circle's job isn't to out-vote them or wear them down -- it's to fold what they know and are bringing forward into a better proposal. A genuine objection makes the resulting decision stronger. A fake one -- "I just don't like it" -- has nowhere to land.
Once the idea has been circulated around the room enough times that everyone is genuinely satisfied, or at least comfortable with moving forward, the circle effects consensus, the plan is adopted (usually with a set period of time for implementation before revisiting to see how it's working, which also helps alleviate pressure: there's a pre-planned exit ramp if the new plan turns out to not be going well); it's communicated to others, and implementation begins.
Now look at what's _**not**_ there: No voting. No hierarchy. No divisiveness; no factions; no knock-down-drag-out fight. No bullying veto. No external interests. No domination; no resentment. No incentive to lie. No incentive to smear or demean.
Every reason to work together. Every voice valued. Every challenge or objection incorporated as the helpful and important information that it is.
It's... transformative, frankly.
Then comes the design that lets this model scale, and I think it's genuinely beautiful. Every circle has a domain -- a sphere of authority that is truly its own. And one rule governs the entire system: **no circle takes an action that damages another circle 's sphere of authority. **Not the small circles, not the big ones.
Authority is nested -- circles within circles -- and coherence is never stamped down from a control center at the top, because there is no control center at the top. Coherence _emerges_ , collaboratively, from the bottom, because each part is whole and each part is honored.

### **How does this actually scale?**
It's surprisingly simple.
From each circle, two people - the "double links" \- also participate in the circle at the next level of coordination. (Two people, to share the load, ensure honesty and clarity, and for redundancy in case of illness or incapacity.)
A simple example: one circle is responsible for the domain of the Accounting department, with full authority and responsibility for decisions that affect that work. Another circle is responsible for Outreach. Another one, for Maintenance. No circle interferes in another's work, and two representatives from each of those circles **also participate** in the General Operations circle that provides overall coordination and support (formerly known as "management") across those departments.
Because of the consent structure, in which objections are never overridden and proposals only move forward with everyone's consent, and because of the presence of the "double links," **nothing the General Operations circle decides will ever damage the work of the Accounting, Outreach, and Maintenance circles.**
And from the General Operations circle, two people _also_ participate in the Company Strategy circle, at the next level of organization above that. That could be the upper boundary of the system; there might be no direct circles interlinking with that one - or, perhaps... from the Company Strategy circle, one could imagine two participants at the City Council circle and maybe someone also serves on the support circle for the neighboring school; from the City Council, up to the County Council and the Bioregional Watershed circles, and... you get my drift.

## **Why I keep calling it fun**
Let me savor this with you a moment, because this is the part nobody believes until they've felt it.
I have sat in these rooms (and Zoom meetings). With and without sociocracy, and the difference is stark. People think sociocracy is fringe, but it's actually **so** much better than our standard ways of working together - which tend towards competition, hierarchy, suppression, and demotivation.
I have run sociocratic processes with real money, real projects, and real stakes on the table. And what happens is initially slow, slightly surprising, then shockingly peaceful.
The divisiveness drains out. The performance of toughness -- the chest-puffing, the point-scoring, the my-way-or-the-highway -- just stops being useful, so people stop doing it.
The resentment that curdles a majority-rule meeting, where half the room leaves having lost? Gone, because nobody got steamrolled.
The furious person who can hijack an entire evening? Their refusal only carries weight if it's reasoned and real -- and if it's real, it improves the outcome; and if it isn't, it dissolves.
And that low, constant pressure to conform -- to not be the difficult one, to swallow your true objection just so the meeting can finally end -- that lifts too, because the whole method is built to want your objection, your point of view, your perspective and your lived experience, because it's important.
Because **you are important.**
What's left, when all that poison evaporates, is something I can only call joy. People laugh. They think out loud. They change their minds in public without shame -- one of the rarest and most beautiful things you will ever watch a human being do.
You get real, practical progress, decisions that actually _hold_ because everyone had a genuine hand in them, and you get there faster than the cynics swear is possible.
Once you've learned a few basic moves and you're truly in it, it stops feeling like a technique at all. It feels like the most natural thing in the world -- like this is how we were always meant to decide things together, and somewhere along the way we simply forgot.

## **I 'm not selling you a utopia**
I've read too much history and sat in too many real rooms to trust anyone who does. So let me be honest about where this has actually been tried -- the wins and the losses both.
**Ireland** has used citizens' assemblies for years, on questions from marriage to climate to the amendment that opened the door to its 2018 referendum. But in 2024, Irish voters turned around and rejected two constitutional amendments that grew out of an assembly process. A real defeat. And the arguments about why -- did interest groups steer the agenda? did the government garble what the assembly actually recommended? -- point straight at the same lesson from either direction: the chain from what ordinary people decide to what finally lands on the ballot has to be transparent and faithful, or the whole thing rots from the middle. We'll get into that in a moment.
**British Columbia** , in 2004, did something no government had ever done: it handed a body of randomly chosen citizens the authority to recommend a wholesale change to a state's electoral system. 160 residents, drawn by lottery from every riding, met roughly every other weekend for a year -- a twelve-week learning phase, then over 50 public hearings and 1,603 written submissions, then deliberation. They voted 146 to 7 to recommend replacing first-past-the-post with a single transferable vote, and it went straight to the public in a referendum.
And now hold onto something.
That proposal carried a majority in 77 of British Columbia's 79 electoral districts. It won 57.7% of the province-wide vote. And it failed -- because the legislature had set the threshold at 60%.
I want you to sit with that, because I have lived the small version of it. I told you in my last essay that I won 59.57% of an endorsement vote in a legislative district this year, and received nothing, because the threshold had been set at 60%. A province of five million people ran into the identical wall on the identical question -- whether ordinary people should get more power -- and lost by the identical margin.
That is what a supermajority gate is for. It is the most elegant instrument ever devised for making a clear majority mean nothing, while letting everyone involved insist the process was perfectly fair. It works the same in a church basement in Auburn as it does across a Canadian province. And it is always, always aimed the same direction: at whoever is trying to move power outward.
**East Belgium** built something sturdier than a one-off. The German-speaking community there -- about 78,000 people -- created a permanent deliberative body in 2019: a standing Citizens' Council of two dozen randomly selected residents, which sets the agenda and convenes citizens' assemblies on the issues it chooses. Members rotate off. Nobody accumulates. It never hardens into another permanent political class, because the architecture won't let it. It's the closest thing in the world to what I'm actually proposing -- and it has been running, quietly, for years, in a community smaller than Kent, Washington.
That's the proof I keep coming back to. This isn't a thought experiment. It's a functioning institution. It's just not _here_.
**France** convened 150 randomly selected citizens on climate -- a Convention drawn by lottery from a pool of 300,000 randomly generated phone numbers, sorted to mirror the country by age, gender, class, education, region. Truck drivers, farmers, nurses. They were paid the same daily rate as a juror. They met over seven sessions across nine months and produced 149 measures -- the crime of "ecocide," mandatory energy-efficient housing renovation, a ban on advertising for heavily polluting goods, a constitutional guarantee for biodiversity. And they did it while telling the experts no: a carbon tax was pressed on them at every turn by the specialists and by the President himself, and they rejected it -- one of them snapping at an expert, "don't treat us like children." So much for the theory that ordinary people can't help but be led.
Macron had promised their proposals would go forward sans filtre -- "without filter." He committed to 146 of the 149. Then the lobbyists went to work in the ministries and the parliament, and the citizens' proposals were watered down and stripped out of the bill that was supposed to carry them. One assessment put the share that survived intact at around 10%. The people did their job magnificently. The machine ate the homework.
That is the failure mode I most want us to design against, and I'll come back to it in a moment.
None of this is fringe. The OECD has been cataloguing these processes for years; its database now holds 733 cases across 34 countries -- and from 1979 through 2023, at least 80,622 people have been chosen by lottery to sit in one of them. The permanent, institutionalized ones -- the ones written into the architecture rather than convened once and dissolved -- nearly doubled between 2020 and 2023, from 22 to 41, most of them at the local and regional level.
The wave is already here. America is simply standing with its back to it.

## **Now let me tell you exactly how this gets stolen**
I said I wouldn't sell you a utopia, so let me show you precisely how a system like this gets gutted -- because it has been, and the elites who did it were smiling the whole time.
**Whoever writes the question has already half-decided the answer.**
In 1999, Australia held a referendum on becoming a republic -- on cutting the last cord to the British Crown and having an Australian head of state instead of a monarch on the other side of the planet. And for most of that decade, a solid majority of Australians wanted exactly that. _Measured_ support ran consistently above 70% - folks who lived there felt like the true number was 95%. Republicans outnumbered monarchists roughly two to one.
This should have been the easiest thing in the world.
It wasn't -- because of how the question was built.
The model that went on that ballot came out of a Constitutional Convention where **half the delegates were appointed by the government instead of elected** -- convened by a Prime Minister who was himself a monarchist, and who then campaigned against his own referendum. Out of that room came exactly one option, put to the people as a take-it-or-leave-it: a republic whose president would be _appointed by two-thirds of Parliament._
But most Australian republicans didn't want a president handed to them by politicians. They wanted to _elect_ their own head of state -- by better than two to one, in the polling of the day.
So the opposition did something cynical and brilliant. It told direct-election republicans to vote "No" _because_ they were republicans. Call it a "politicians' republic." Reject this one, hold out for a better one, we'll do it right next time.
The strategy worked. The referendum failed, 54.87% to 45.13%, and the threshold needed to be 60%. It lost in every single state. Australia is still a monarchy today, twenty-seven years later, and **no serious second attempt has ever come.**
A clear majority wanted the change. They were handed a question engineered so that their majority could not express itself.
Now hold that up next to **Brexit** , which went wrong in precisely the opposite direction. There, the word on the ballot -- "Leave" -- was never defined at all. It meant leave the single market, or stay in it, or something else entirely, depending on which voter you asked. A vague question gathered up incompatible hopes into one number and called it a mandate. And the country then spent years in chaos, discovering that its people had voted for entirely different futures under the same word.
Too specific, and you fracture the majority that agreed on the goal. Too vague, and you manufacture a mandate that nobody actually gave. Both are ways of extracting a verdict from the public while never giving the public a real choice.
This is what I need you to see, because it's the pattern under every single failure in this essay:
**The danger has never been that ordinary people can 't govern. The danger is always that the people who already hold power keep control of the question, the witness list, and the follow-through.**
Look at them again. Australia -- half the delegates appointed, and a question engineered to split the majority. France -- 149 proposals from ordinary citizens, promised implementation _without filter_ , then quietly dismembered by lobbyists in the ministries. British Columbia -- a supermajority gate set by the establishment _just high enough_ that 57.7% of an entire province amounted to nothing. Ireland -- a chain of custody, from the assembly's recommendation to the words finally printed on the ballot, that nobody could vouch for.
**Not one of those was a failure of the citizens.**
Every single one was a failure of the powerful to keep their word.
So if we build this, we build it with the locks on:
* **Independent framing.** The question cannot be written by the officials who convened the council. And the council must have standing power to amend or reject its own charge. If a hundred and fifty ordinary people study a problem for six months and conclude that they were asked the wrong question, they must be able to say so, on the record, and send it back.
* **Their own witnesses.** The council calls whoever it wants to hear from. A briefing binder assembled entirely by the people who commissioned the study isn't evidence. It's a framed curriculum.
* **A duty to answer.** Government must respond publicly, in writing, on a clock, to every recommendation -- and where it refuses one, it must say why, in its own name, signed, where you can read it.
* **Real thresholds.** _Simple majorities decide_. A supermajority gate is not a safeguard; it is a thumb on the scale, and it is always, always pressing down on the side of existing powers.

I know exactly how that last one sounds, coming from me. I lost an endorsement this year with 59.57% of the vote against a 60% threshold. British Columbia lost an entire electoral system with 57.7% against that same number. Believe me when I tell you I have thought about that particular arithmetic more than most people ever will.
None of these dangers go away by pretending they aren't real. So I won't.

## **None of this is new**
Here's what surprised me most when I started pulling the thread. We talk about ordinary people governing themselves as if it were some untested startup idea. **It is very nearly the oldest political technology our species has.**
The Athenians -- who handed us the word _democracy_ -- didn't mostly elect their officials. They drew them by lot. **They regarded election as the aristocratic method, the tool of the wealthy and the well-known, and the lottery as the democratic one, precisely because a lottery can 't be campaigned for or bought.** Sortition isn't a break from democracy's roots. It _is_ democracy's roots.
In the Muslim tradition I've come home to, governing by consultation isn't a footnote -- it's a command. _Wa amruhum sh ūrā baynahum_ -- "their affairs are decided by consultation among them." _Wa sh āwirhum fī'l-amr _-- "and consult them in the matter." And it was that civilization, across some fourteen centuries, that carried and enlarged the inheritance of Greece -- the mathematics, the medicine, the optics, the philosophy -- through Europe's long Dark Ages and handed it forward, giving direct birth to the Renaissance.
Long before Europeans wrote a word of governance on this American continent, the indigenous Haudenosaunee -- the Six Nations -- lived under the Great Law of Peace: nested councils, decisions reached by consensus, leaders chosen _**and unseated**_ by the clan mothers, and a principle we would be wise to carve over the door of every legislature on earth -- that you weigh each decision against its effect on the seventh generation yet to come.
In the Horn of Africa, the Oromo people built the Gadaa system -- a democracy organized in generational classes, authority handed peacefully to a new set of leaders every eight years, with hard limits on how long anyone could hold power. Term limits and the graceful handoff I called for in my last essay -- worked out on the African plateau centuries before our Constitution was signed.
And the consent method I described, deciding together without a vote that crushes the minority? The Quakers have practiced their own version for three hundred years, listening in their meetings for what they call the _sense of the meeting_ - an emerging sense of agreement - rather than tallying winners and losers.
Athens and Baghdad and the Haudenosaunee longhouse and the Gadaa assembly and the Quaker meeting house do not share a religion, a continent, or a century. What they share is an intuition our own moment has very nearly lost: **that a people 's affairs belong to the people**, and that ordinary human beings, gathered under the right conditions, can govern ourselves with wisdom.
This is the basic concept of self-governance - the visionary experiment that started America.
Set all of that beside the distorted and abusive thing we've been trained to call "democracy" -- _pick a professional every few years off a menu two private clubs approved, then go home and watch_ -- and our version starts to look less like the natural order of the universe and more like the strange, recent, narrow, and highly unappealing exception it actually is.

## **What I am actually proposing**
"Wouldn't it be nice" is not a policy, and you deserve better than a daydream. So let me be specific.
I am not proposing we abolish Congress tomorrow and pull 535 names from a hat. Elections do real things we can't live without -- they let us choose a direction, compare ideologies and approaches, and, just as importantly, throw people out by name when they fail us. We should keep that. We need it.
What I'm proposing is that we finally build the other half -- the half we've been missing: **a real Citizens ' Council system, standing alongside the bodies we already elect.**
Start where people live -- at the county level. (Or even closer to home.) Build it out at the state level, in partnership with State legislatures. Then convene circles at the federal level. And there's no reason in principle it has to stop at a city line or a national border; the same nested logic could run from a neighborhood all the way up to problems that are frankly planetary - wherever the people want to take it.
Councils of ordinary residents, drawn by civic lottery to mirror the actual public, seated for limited terms with real pay and real support so it's never just a rich person's hobby. No campaigns. No fundraising. No reelection to angle for. No donor to please.
Organized the way I described -- nested circles, each with a genuine domain, deciding by consent, bound by that one unbreakable rule that no circle acts in a way that wrecks another's sphere of authority.
**Coherence** that emerges naturally instead of **compliance** that's commanded and forced.
And give these councils real teeth: the power to put a question on the public agenda, to force a recorded vote, to call their own witnesses, to send legislation back with a written finding when it reeks of capture -- and, in some matters, to decide outright.
Built with the locks I described above -- independent framing, their own witnesses, a duty to answer, honest thresholds -- because a Citizens' Council without those is just a very expensive listening session, and I refuse to design one of those and pretend it's power.
Then pair them, always, with the government we elect, the two halves checking and completing each other. Representativeness from the lottery. Accountability from the ballot.
That -- not a slogan on a yard sign -- is what **no corporate PACs, no foreign interests, no defense contractors** looks like once you build it all the way down into the architecture.
You cannot buy a legislator whose name doesn't exist until they're drawn, who can't run again, whose service simply ends. Capture needs a permanent, knowable class to sink its hooks into. This dissolves the handhold.

## **The pledge I 've been carrying**
I have a tattoo in the middle of my back, over my heart, where I can't see it and mostly forget it's there.
It's a pattern of overlapping circles -- the kind that nest inside one another and tessellate outward forever, the way they do in the geometry of the beehive, where a single unity radiates into endless coherent order, the same figure holding true at every scale. Inside it, I carry the Oak of Gernika -- the tree under which the Basques, the last surviving indigenous people of mainland Europe, swore generation after generation, to keep faith with their own liberties. It's the living sign that legitimate power is rooted in a _place_ , and in a _covenant_ , and in a living world that will outlast every one of us.
For years, I described its meaning as "democracy in partnership with nature." That's true. But I understand it far better now than I did the day I chose it.
I did not have the words, back then, for the vision I was marking into my skin. I have them now -- and they came from a governance handbook and a fourteen-hundred-year-old verse and a longhouse and a meeting for worship, all saying the same thing my soul has been drawn to the whole time: that **power should be organized the way living things are organized**. Nested. Reciprocal. Rooted in place. Self-correcting. Whole at every scale. With no single center it can't survive losing.
I was carrying the architecture on my own body before I could name it. And I suspect you've been carrying some version of it too. Most people have. We were simply taught to stop expecting it from our government.
But governments are living things too.

## **So I 'm not going to ask you to adopt a plank**
I'm going to ask you to let a door swing open.
We already trust twelve or twenty-four strangers with a person's freedom. We built a whole solemn architecture -- the jury -- on the faith that ordinary people, given the facts and the time and the duty to reason together, will mostly find their way to justice.
Let's learn from our shared humanity, our shared memory, and the best of what human civilization has developed - so we can build something which will continue to serve freedom, justice, and peace long after we are gone.
I'll leave you with one question. It's a question we have been very carefully trained not to ask:
**If we trust ordinary people with a human being 's liberty in a courtroom, why have we decided we can't trust them with the ordinary business of governing their own lives?**
Sit with it. That's all I'm asking today -- not that you sign onto a bill, but that you let yourself feel the door open before anyone asks you to walk through it. Because once you've really seen it -- once you understand that you were never meant to be merely the audience -- the way things are begins to look a great deal stranger than the way things could be.
